subjects.name: Indian Polity
subjects.description: Indian Constitution, System of Government, and Constitutional Organs

units.name: Unit 1: Constitutional Framework
units.description: Historical background, making of the constitution, preamble, and salient features

cards.heading: Historical Foundations
cards.body: The constitutional framework of India evolved through various British-era legislative acts. Key milestones include the Regulating Act of 1773, Charter Acts, and the Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935.
cards.tip: The Government of India Act 1935 contributed the majority of the administrative blueprint.

recapQuestions.questionText: Which act established the dual control system of double government?
recapQuestions.explanation: Pitt's India Act of 1784 separated political affairs (managed by Board of Control) and commercial affairs (managed by Court of Directors).

questions.questionText: The Federal Court of India was established in which year under the Act of 1935?
questions.explanation: The Federal Court of India was set up in 1937 in Delhi under the provisions of the Government of India Act 1935.

modules.name: Module 0: Unit 1 Summary
modules.description: Comprehensive key milestones and summaries of the entire Constitutional Framework

lessons.name: Unit 1 Master Summary
lessons.description: Quick review deck spanning historical rules to constitution drafting

cards.heading: Master Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson summarizes the entire Unit 1 content. It covers the evolution from East India Company rules to the final adoption of the Constitution on November 26, 1949.
cards.tip: Use this card as a high-level table of contents.

cards.heading: Milestone 1: Company Rule (1773-1858)
cards.body: Parliament gradually took control over the East India Company via the Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act 1784, and the final Charter Act of 1853 which separated legislative and executive organs.
cards.tip: The EIC began as a trading venture and ended as a pure administrative body.

cards.heading: Milestone 2: Crown Rule (1858-1947)
cards.body: Direct British Empire control started in 1858. The Secretary of State and Viceroy offices were created. Morley-Minto 1909 introduced separate electorates; Montagu-Chelmsford 1919 brought dyarchy; and the 1935 Act proposed a federation.
cards.tip: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy.

cards.heading: Milestone 3: Drafting the Constitution
cards.body: The Constituent Assembly sat for almost 3 years. It adopted the Objectives Resolution and set up the Drafting Committee chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to create the supreme law.
cards.tip: The assembly acted as both a constituent and legislative body.

cards.heading: Milestone 4: Core Pillars Adopted
cards.body: On November 26, 1949, the Constitution was adopted with 395 Articles and 8 Schedules. Full enforcement occurred on January 26, 1950, commemorating Purna Swaraj Day.
cards.tip: Parts of citizenship and elections were enforced immediately in Nov 1949.

cards.heading: Company vs Crown
cards.body:
The historical background is divided into: 
1. **Company Rule (1773-1858)**: Regulating, Pitt's, and Charter Acts.
2. **Crown Rule (1858-1947)**: Government of India Acts and Councils Acts.

questions.questionText: Which act introduced separate electorates for Muslims?
questions.explanation: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

lessons.name: Module 1 Summary
lessons.description: 5-card master summary of the historical evolution

cards.heading: Module 1 Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson summarizes the historical acts under British rule. It highlights the transformation of India's administrative architecture from 1773 to 1947.
cards.tip: Use this as a quick reference timeline guide.

cards.heading: Centralization Trend (1773-1833)
cards.body: Centralization started with Warren Hastings as Governor-General of Bengal (1773) and reached its peak with Lord William Bentinck becoming Governor-General of India (1833) with full legislative controls.
cards.tip: The 1833 Charter ended the EIC commercial monopoly completely.

cards.heading: Decentralization Trend (1861-1937)
cards.body: Decentralization began with the Indian Councils Act of 1861, restoring legislative powers to Bombay and Madras presidencies, culminating in provincial autonomy under the 1935 Act.
cards.tip: Provincial autonomy came into force in 1937.

cards.heading: Communal Electorates Evolution
cards.body: Lord Minto introduced separate electorates for Muslims in 1909. This communal electorate system was extended to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans in 1919.
cards.tip: Lord Minto is known as the Father of Communal Electorate.

cards.heading: Double Government Systems
cards.body: Pitt's India Act of 1784 established a system of double government. In 1919, a system of dual rule called dyarchy (transferred and reserved subjects) was introduced in provinces.
cards.tip: Dyarchy in provinces was abolished by the 1935 Act.

lessons.name: The Company Rule (1773–1858)
lessons.description: Overview of British parliamentary control over the East India Company

cards.heading: Lesson 1 Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson reviews Company Rule from 1773 to 1858. It covers the Regulating Act of 1773, Pitt's India Act of 1784, and the final Charter Acts.
cards.tip: Focus on the transition of power from EIC to the Crown.

cards.heading: The Regulating Act of 1773
cards.body: First step by the British Government to regulate the Company. It designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings) and set up the Calcutta Supreme Court.
cards.tip: Warren Hastings was assisted by a 4-member executive council.

cards.heading: Pitt’s India Act of 1784
cards.body: Distinguished between commercial (Court of Directors) and political (Board of Control) functions, establishing a double government.
cards.tip: Company territories were termed 'British possessions in India'.

lessons.name: The Crown Rule (1858–1947)
lessons.description: Direct administration by the British Empire and constitutional developments

cards.heading: Lesson 2 Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson reviews the Crown Rule from 1858 to 1947. Learn about the Secretary of State, Morley-Minto, Montagu-Chelmsford, and the 1935 Government of India Act.
cards.tip: Compare provincial dyarchy of 1919 with central dyarchy of 1935.

cards.heading: Government of India Act 1858
cards.body: Transferred EIC territories and administration to the British Crown. Replaced Governor-General with Viceroy (Lord Canning) and created the Secretary of State for India.
cards.tip: Abolished Board of Control and Court of Directors.

cards.heading: Government of India Act 1935
cards.body: Divided powers into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent lists. Abolished provincial dyarchy, introduced provincial autonomy, and established a Federal Court.
cards.tip: The All-India Federation proposed in this act never materialized.

modules.name: Module 2: Making of the Constitution
modules.description: How the Constituent Assembly was formed, drafted, and enacted the supreme law

lessons.name: Module 2 Summary
lessons.description: 5-card master summary of assembly workings and drafts

cards.heading: Module 2 Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson summarizes how the Constitution was designed. We highlight the Cabinet Mission plan, major committees, and the final adoption of the draft.
cards.tip: Keep key dates (December 1946, November 1949) in mind.

cards.heading: The Assembly Genesis (Nov 1946)
cards.body: Constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan. It consisted of 389 members initially, reduced to 299 after Partition. First meeting was on December 9, 1946.
cards.tip: Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha was temporary president.

cards.heading: Objectives Resolution
cards.body: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic Objectives Resolution on Dec 13, 1946. It laid the ideological base of the constitution and became the Preamble.
cards.tip: Adopted unanimously on Jan 22, 1947.

cards.heading: The Drafting Committee
cards.body: Chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. It was a 7-member committee appointed on August 29, 1947, to write the draft based on reports of other advisory panels.
cards.tip: Ambedkar is called the Father of the Indian Constitution.

cards.heading: Enactment & Adoption
cards.body: Adopted on November 26, 1949. Contained 395 Articles and 8 Schedules. Full commencement was on January 26, 1950, to mark the Lahore Congress Purna Swaraj resolution date.
cards.tip: January 26 is celebrated as Republic Day.

lessons.name: Composition and Working of Assembly
lessons.description: How the assembly represented India and handled legislative work

cards.heading: Lesson 1 Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson outlines the composition, seat allocation, and key meetings of the Constituent Assembly.
cards.tip: Note that seats were allocated based on population (1 per million).

cards.heading: Seat Allocation and Partition
cards.body: Seats allocated to British Provinces and Princely States. Following Partition, members representing Pakistan territories withdrew, reducing the count to 299.
cards.tip: Assembly members were indirectly elected by provincial assemblies.

units.name: Unit 2: System of Government
units.description: Parliamentary system, federal features, emergency powers, and relations

modules.name: Module 0: Unit 2 Summary
modules.description: Master summaries on Parliamentary Systems and Federal Organs

lessons.name: Unit 2 Master Summary
lessons.description: 5-card master summary of System of Government

cards.heading: Unit 2 Overview
cards.body: This lesson summarizes parliamentary features, executive accountability, and federal versus unitary distributions of power in the Indian System of Government.
cards.tip: Focus on the separation of legislative and executive powers.

cards.heading: Parliamentary Government
cards.body: India adopted the Westminster model at both Centre and States. Key features are executive responsibility to the legislature, dual executives (nominal and real), and leadership of the Prime Minister.
cards.tip: Article 74 & 75 outline parliamentary structure at the Centre.

cards.heading: Federal Structure
cards.body: India's system is federal with a strong unitary bias (described as 'quasi-federal'). Unitary characteristics include a single constitution, emergency powers, and appointment of Governors.
cards.tip: Article 1 describes India as a Union of States.

cards.heading: Relations (Centre & States)
cards.body: Legislative relations (Article 245-255), administrative relations (Article 256-263), and financial relations allocate authority clearly but allow central dominance during emergencies.
cards.tip: The concurrent list covers shared jurisdictions.

cards.heading: Emergency Powers
cards.body: Part XVIII of the Constitution (Articles 352-360) grants emergency powers to safeguard the country's sovereignty. During emergencies, the federal structure turns unitary.
cards.tip: No financial emergency has ever been declared in India.

modules.name: Module 3: Parliamentary System
modules.description: The Westminster model of government and executive-legislative balance

cards.heading: Module 3 Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson summarizes the Parliamentary Westminster system. It covers nominal vs real executives, collective responsibility, and political homogeneity.
cards.tip: Contrast this with the presidential model of separate powers.

cards.heading: Nominal and Real Executives
cards.body: The President is the nominal executive (De Jure head) while the Prime Minister is the real executive (De Facto head) who exercises supreme powers.
cards.tip: The PM leads the Council of Ministers.

cards.heading: Collective Responsibility
cards.body: Ministers are collectively responsible to the Parliament, specifically the Lok Sabha (Lower House). They sink or swim together (No-Confidence Motion).
cards.tip: This is the core pillar of parliamentary accountability.

cards.heading: Political Homogeneity
cards.body: Members of the Council of Ministers usually belong to the same political party or coalition, sharing similar policies and administrative vision.
cards.tip: In coalition cabinets, this is achieved through a common minimum program.

cards.heading: Double Membership
cards.body: Ministers must be members of Parliament. If a non-MP is appointed as a minister, they must secure a seat within 6 months.
cards.tip: This ensures the executive remains rooted inside the legislature.

lessons.name: Features of Parliamentary Government
lessons.description: Core pillars including executive accountability and leadership

cards.heading: Lesson 1 Summary Overview
cards.body: This lesson covers the primary features of the parliamentary executive in India.
cards.tip: Note the leadership role of the Prime Minister.

cards.heading: Prime Minister Leadership
cards.body: The Prime Minister acts as the leader of the council, leader of the parliament, and leader of the ruling party, coordinating all government organs.
cards.tip: Ambedkar described the PM as the pivot of the entire administration.
